subject: What happens to session requests & exports — quick lifecycle + deletion steps
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@finlytics.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sun, 12 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question — what gets included in a chat export?

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is working through our security checklist and asked a practical question: when we export a session for e-discovery or audit, what exactly is included by default? Specifically:

- Do exports include the original user "prompt" text and the model "response"?
- Are streaming fragments or intermediate tokens captured?
- Do embeddings / model metadata (e.g., model version, quantization profile) come with the export?

Also, if we request deletion of a session, what is the expected timeline and confirmation we receive? Our legal team wants to show a deletion proof path in the contract.

Appreciate a short checklist we can attach to the security questionnaire.

— Rajiv
FinLytics — Head of Security Operations

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sun, 12 May 2029 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question — what gets included in a chat export?

Rajiv — thanks for the clear questions. I put a concise answer below (so you can paste into the questionnaire) and attached a short runbook for procurement. High level first, then details.

TL;DR (short checklist you can paste):
- Exports include: full request (what user sent), full response (final model output as returned to user), model metadata (model name and version), request-level headers (region, timestamp), and export audit stamp.
- Streaming fragments are NOT included by default in exports — only the final assembled response is exported.
- KV/prefix cache artifacts are considered transient and are not included; embeddings created and stored as a separate product (if enabled) are available but only if you explicitly request an embeddings export.
- Default hosted retention window: 30 days for request/response artifacts; customers may opt for longer retention via Dedicated/Private plans or by enabling retention + archive add-ons. Deletion requests for hosted accounts are executed within 48 hours of verification and a confirmation is returned.

Details / caveats:
1) Prompts vs outputs: We treat the inbound payload (prompt) and the model's final output as exportable artifacts. If a response was assembled via streaming, only the final response text that the SDK/API returned is recorded for exports.

2) Intermediate artifacts: Token-level streaming fragments, runtime-only KV cache, and prefetch tensors are ephemeral and are not stored in export bundles. We log that streaming occurred (boolean flag) but not the fragments.

3) Embeddings & derivatives: If you use Redwood Embeddings as a managed feature, embeddings are stored in a separate store. Exports of embeddings are opt-in and show up as a dedicated CSV/ndjson export.

4) Model metadata: Model name, pinned version, and serving quantization profile are included in export metadata so auditors can reproduce results. We do not include low-level binary artifacts or compiled kernels.

5) Deletion workflow (hosted): Customer submits a deletion ticket via the console or API -> Redwood verifies ownership and scope -> hosted logs/exports/prompt-response artifacts for the requested session are purged from primary stores within 48 hours and tombstoned from backups per the normal backup cycle (up to additional 7 days) -> A signed deletion confirmation (PDF) is provided. For Dedicated/Private we provide the deletion runbook and can coordinate SLA terms.

Attached: Retention-Export-Guide-FinLytics.pdf and data-deletion-runbook-v1.2.pdf (runbook contains step-by-step API calls for on-demand purge).

If helpful I can give you the exact API sample to call (we use a DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/artifacts call + verification token).

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick question — what gets included in a chat export?

Adding a couple of operational notes we often hear from procurements so Rajiv can keep them in his packet:

- Export formats: JSON bundle (requests/responses + metadata) or ndjson for large exports; embeddings come as ndjson/CSV.
- Audit trail: Every export gets a signed audit entry with timestamp, initiator identity (console user or API key id), and IP range. We recommend including that audit stamp in your retention policy appendix.
- Residency: Exports are generated from the region where the session ran. If FinLytics pins sessions to eu-west-1, export data will be assembled and retained per the EU region rules (we can produce an SCC checklist for that).
- Proof-of-deletion: For hosted accounts we provide two items: API deletion confirmation (id + timestamp) and a signed PDF summary for legal.

Rajiv — happy to hop on a quick call if your legal wants to walk through the exact verbiage.

— Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Data Governance | Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene / Marissa — this is exactly what we needed.

A couple quick follow-ups from procurement / legal:
- Can you confirm the hosted default window in writing (you mentioned 30 days)? We need that spelled out in the MSA appendix.
- For the 48-hour deletion window: does that apply to exports generated previously (i.e., purge both stored artifacts and any previously downloaded export files that remain in our workspace)?

If you can send a one-paragraph statement we can insert into the appendix, procurement will move forward with the SOW. If easier, we can sign the runbook NDA and run through the API steps in a joint session.

— Rajiv
